❗️The AI domain war has officially begun

OpenAI, Google and Meta are now fighting over some of the most valuable AI-related internet domains.

ICANN received 1,615 applications from 481 applicants in its first new domain expansion since 2012. OpenAI applied for 15 domains, including .agent, .agi, .asi, .chatgpt, .gpt, .mcp, .model and .openai.

Google went even bigger with 39 applications, including .agent, .mcp, .gemini, .deepmind and .api. Meta submitted 18, including .agent, .llama, .metaai and .superintelligence.

Some strings are already crowded: .agent has 13 applicants, .agi has 7, and .mcp has 5. Interestingly, Anthropic, which created MCP didn’t apply for .mcp at all.

Anthropic only applied for .anthropic and .claude, while Microsoft went for .copilot and .msft.

Each application costs $227,000, and contested domains can become extremely expensive. Google previously paid $25 million for .app.

The process could continue until 2030, and none of these domains has been awarded yet.

⚠️ AI’s “Mathocalypse” could threaten internet security

OpenAI’s AI models are making rapid progress in mathematics. The company recently released 722 mathematical manuscripts covering 372 result families, reporting advances across roughly 4,000 longstanding problems.

Computer scientist Scott Aaronson called the wave of breakthroughs a “Mathocalypse.” 👀

AI could eventually help discover algorithms capable of breaking public-key cryptography, which protects online banking, private messages and cryptocurrency.

Ethereum researcher Justin Drake has urged the blockchain industry to prepare for “bunker mode.”

AI hasn’t broken modern encryption, but if mathematical discoveries accelerate, the race to secure the internet could become much more urgent.

❗️AI companies are preparing for a catastrophic incident as early as 2027

Executives at OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies are reportedly bracing for a public and political backlash following a major AI-related disaster, according to Axios.

Industry insiders reportedly expect a serious incident within the next 6–12 months, potentially involving an AI-powered cyberattack that disrupts banking, internet access, electricity or water supplies.

OpenAI confirmed that it conducts preparedness exercises, while stressing that such scenarios are not considered inevitable. The goal, according to the company, is to prepare for a range of possible circumstances.

Anthropic declined to comment.

🇨🇳 China Is giving AI-generated humans government IDs

China is taking virtual influencers beyond social media. AI-generated digital humans are reportedly receiving state-issued identity cards that could allow them to open digital-currency wallets, sign contracts and enter commercial partnerships.

One of the first is Yuri, a virtual idol and artist recognized as a “digital resident” in Beijing. The IDs reportedly include personal details such as a name, birthday, address and facial features.

The move comes as China’s digital-human industry expands, with more than 1.3 million active businesses and a reported market value exceeding $10 billion.

Supporters say the system could protect intellectual property and make the companies behind virtual personas legally accountable. Critics warn it could also extend state surveillance into digital identities. Meanwhile, some firms are reportedly offering people up to $20,000 to license their likenesses for AI-generated replicas.

China’s experiment could become an early test of how governments regulate AI identities as virtual entities begin participating in the economy.

⚠️ AI may have helped discover a planet hiding in NASA data since 2018

An independent researcher used Claude Code to identify a possible new exoplanet buried in NASA’s TESS data since 2018, with no earlier report of the candidate found by the researcher.

Claude Code, powered by Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1, handled much of the technical work: analyzing stellar brightness data, searching for transits, fitting the signals and ruling out potential false positives. The researcher defined the questions and criteria for validating the result.

The candidate orbits a star roughly 116 light-years away. Every 3.18 days, the star dims by around 0.05% for about two hours, a pattern consistent with a planet approximately 1.4 times the size of Earth.

It’s not a confirmed discovery yet. NASA’s TESS mission is scheduled to observe the system again from October 31 to November 26, potentially providing more evidence.

🇺🇸 Trump Calls Elon Musk a “National Treasure” and Modern-Day Thomas Edison

President Donald Trump publicly praised Elon Musk, describing him as one of the greatest technology founders in history and a person who has done more to advance America’s national interests than most.

Trump highlighted Musk’s work at SpaceX, crediting the company with reducing NASA’s reliance on foreign space programs, developing Starship and building Starlink into a global satellite network.

He also recalled how he contacted Musk during a hurricane in North Carolina, claiming Starlink equipment arrived within hours and helped save hundreds of lives when communities were cut off from communications.

Trump praised Tesla for advancing electric vehicles and described Neuralink’s work on restoring sight, speech and movement as another example of Musk’s technological ambition. He also called Musk a leader in superintelligence.

“Elon is our modern-day Thomas Edison,” Trump declared, ending his remarks by calling Musk a “national treasure” and congratulating him on his achievements.

🥺 Sam Altman says AI reasoning is moving into a new league

In a conversation with Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff, Sam Altman described a striking progression in AI’s mathematical abilities.

GPT-5.5 was compared to an average math professor, GPT-5.6 to the top 1–2%, and Astra to a level slightly beyond that. Altman reportedly said OpenAI’s next internal model was tackling problems that even top mathematicians struggle with.

If these comparisons hold up, the bigger story isn’t any single benchmark. It’s how quickly the bar keeps rising.

AI is moving beyond answering questions toward solving problems that have challenged experts. The next generation could be a very different beast.

❗️A top mathematician warns against sharing original ideas with ChatGPT

Tristan Buckmaster still uses AI tools but says he no longer shares his original research ideas with OpenAI or Anthropic.

His concern grew after OpenAI published 722 mathematical manuscripts covering 372 families of results, generated using an experimental model unavailable to outside researchers. He fears young mathematicians could see years of work overtaken overnight.

He also warns that grant reviewers sometimes upload research proposals to AI tools, potentially exposing confidential ideas.

OpenAI denies misusing user data, and there’s no proof it took Buckmaster’s work.

His warning: the AI helping you make a breakthrough could belong to a company racing to make that breakthrough first.
